LESSON: READING 6.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION – PLAY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.2: Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play, part of Strand 6 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How can we enhance comprehension when reading a play? 2. How does indigenous trade differ from modern trade?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify vocabulary on indigenous trade from a play for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. summarise the main ideas from a play for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. respond to questions from a play for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. acknowledge relating events and ideas to real life for life-long learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify vocabulary on indigenous trade from a play for information,

   Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. summarise the main ideas from a play for comprehension,

   Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. respond to questions from a play for comprehension,

   Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. acknowledge relating events and ideas to real life for life-long learning.

   Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. conduct a reader’s theatre to read an excerpt of a play on indigenous languages,

2. identify vocabulary related to indigenous trade from the plays read,

3. conduct a spelling bee mini- contest to spell out and read the vocabulary related to the theme,

4. work together to match the new words to their meaning,

5. make notes on the key details from the play,

6. team up to discuss the characteristics of a play with examples from the plays read,

7. write down a summary of the main events from the plays,

8. answer direct and inferential questions from the plays, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. conduct a reader’s theatre to read an excerpt of a play on indigenous languages,
2. identify vocabulary related to indigenous trade from the plays read,
3. conduct a spelling bee mini- contest to spell out and read the vocabulary related to the theme,
4. work together to match the new words to their meaning,
5. make notes on the key details from the play,
6. team up to discuss the characteristics of a play with examples from the plays read,
7. write down a summary of the main events from the plays,
8. answer direct and inferential questions from the plays, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 6.2.1 Reading for comprehension – Play together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The learner jointly conducts a reader’s theatre to read an excerpt of a play on indigenous

languages.

• Critical Thinking and Problem-solving: This is enhanced as the learner analyses concepts logically to match the new words

to their meaning.

Values:
• Unity: The learner cooperates with teams to discuss the characteristics of a play with examples from the plays read.

• Responsibility: The learner diligently conducts a spelling bee mini-contest to spell out and read the vocabulary related to the

theme.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Consumer Awareness: This is acquired as learners interact with texts related to indigenous trade.

Link to other Learning areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of trade to their learning in Social Studies.
